title: Earth Is Closest to the Sun in January #science #space
description:
Earth is closest to the Sun in early January (about 147 million km) and farthest in early July (about 152 million km). So distance can't be why January is cold in the north. Earth's axis is tilted 23.5°: in January the north leans away from the Sun, so sunlight arrives low and weak, spread over more ground.

More on sunlight: Why is the sky blue but sunsets red? https://youtu.be/H_61WImrwoQ

Sources
- NASA Science, APOD 2025 January 4: Welcome to Perihelion (about 147 million km; aphelion about 152 million km)
- NASA NSSDCA, Earth Fact Sheet (perihelion 147.1, aphelion 152.1 million km; eccentricity 0.0167)
- Sunlight on the ground computed: cos(45° + 23.5°) ≈ 0.37 vs cos(45° − 23.5°) ≈ 0.93 at noon in early January
